articles.title: Penny Lane Is Dead review – Aussie slasher comedy zips from Neighbours to nasty
articles.summary: Mia’Kate Russell’s 80s-set Ozsploitation horror is a tad slapdash, but the grungy gore and seething catfights save it from dud status. Here is a muddled if energetic effort from Australian writer-director Mia’Kate Russell.
body: Set in Australia in 1986 (presumably because this means no mobile phones, and thus no calling for help), a trio of high-school besties prepares for a night of partying before the summer ends. Penny (Bailey Spalding) is planning to go to university to study law and asks her girlfriend Toni (Tahlee Fereday) to come with her. The two have only recently become lovers and they haven’t yet come out to their buddy Amy (Alexandra Jensen) – a sweet, childlike teen who still carries a stuffed tiger toy around for comfort.

And they most certainly haven’t come out to Kat (Sophia Wright-Mendelsohn, daughter of Aussie actor Ben Mendelsohn) – an erstwhile friend with whom they haven’t hung out for a while and who they didn’t think would show up that evening. Except here she is, bearing cupcakes for each of them with insults piped on the top in icing. Kat, it turns out, has drugged Penny’s cake, so she passes out and Kat’s super-skeevy ex-con boyfriend Angus (Ben O’Toole) shows up with his leather-clad crew – and suddenly it all goes from an episode of Neighbours to The Last House on the Left.
points: Mia’Kate Russell’s 80s-set Ozsploitation horror is a tad slapdash, but the grungy gore and seething catfights save it from dud status.

articles.title: Zip Wire review – cancer-curing scientist is on the hook for cable-dangle thriller
articles.summary: This nonsensical film sees an OCD-afflicted scientist fending off assassins while hanging from an aerial wire, and fails to get pulses racing for even a minute. In this silly, low-adrenaline thriller, the title star is a rickety old zip wire bolted into the side of a mountain in the Italian…
body: The scientist is Amy (MyAnna Buring); she has discovered a cure for lung cancer, and her drive is explained in syrupy hospital-ward flashbacks to her mother dying when she was a teenager. Amy also has OCD – she is so anxious about germs that she never takes off her rubber gloves, and has an assistant in her lab to do anything that involves touching or handling objects. (Like all the characters, she never gets beyond a stereotype.) Her research is bankrolled by a big pharma company, whose CEO is played by Saffron Burrows (now seemingly mandatory casting for ropey British thrillers).

Amy’s gamechanging discoveries result in an old-school conspiracy, involving a notebook with her research written in code and a trio of contract killers. Which is how Amy ends up in the Dolomites (where everyone has an English accent), halfway across a zip line. Supposedly, a human body cannot remain in a state of maximum panic for more than 30 minutes, but Amy seems to bat away her terrible fear of heights in about five minutes flat. For the audience, you’ll be lucky if this gets your pulse racing for more than two of them.

articles.title: ‘Cairo Conspiracy’s’ Tawfeek Barhom to Star in Les Valseurs’ ‘Borderline’ by Oscar-Nominated Yves Piat (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Palestinian actor Tawfeek Barhom, best known for Tarik Saleh’s Cannes winner “Cairo Conspiracy” in 2022 and Palme d’Or winner 2025 for his short film “I’m Glad You’re Dead Now,” is set to headline the French pic “Borderline” by first-timer Yves Piat.
body: The project is being co-produced by Les Valseurs with Spain’s Sumendi and BTeam, partners to the French outlet on Diego Céspedes’ “ The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo,” (Un Certain Regard top winner in 2025), with funding from Catalonia’s ICEC, France’s CNC, Region Nouvelle-Aquitaine and Pays de la Loire.

The sweeping story is set from the early 1950s in Turkey, through to the disco era in Paris. A boy raised as a girl in Turkey to protect him from a family vendetta, flees to Paris. There he resumes his life as a young man, and overcomes his trauma through creativity as he enters the real of Haute couture.
“We’re in early stages of financing,” said Les Valseurs co-founder who is looking for equity and technical partners.
Both “Borderline” and “All the Softness in the World” are vying for the Storyline Award, Best Pitch and Midpoint Talent Award, to be handed out on Thursday.

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ ‘The Odyssey’ Extend Battle Atop U.K. and Ireland Box Office as ‘Insidious’ Makes Strong Debut
articles.summary: Sony’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” retained the No. 1 spot at the U.K. and Ireland box office for a fourth consecutive week, collecting £3.6 million ($4.8 million), according to Rentrak. The superhero blockbuster pushed its running cumulative gross to $117.9 million.
body: Black Bear’s comedy “ Spa Weekend ” rounded out the top five with an opening haul of $668,191. Paramount’s animated sequel “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie” placed sixth in its third week with $643,678, bringing its cume to $5.9 million.

Mastershot Studios’ Malayalam-language film “Bethlehem Kudumba Unit,” one of India’s Onam holiday releases, landed in seventh place with $593,485. Disney’s animated holdover “Toy Story 5” took eighth position in its 10th week, generating $512,456 to lift its cume to $76.2 million.
Studiocanal’s action thriller “Mutiny” opened in ninth place with $504,397. A24’s “Tony” held the 10th spot in its sophomore session, collecting $461,807 for a total of $1.3 million.

articles.title: Kit Harington replaces Nicholas Hoult in HBO's Harry Potter series
articles.summary: Hoult was announced as Gilderoy Lockhart two weeks ago but has dropped out due to scheduling issues.
body: Kit Harington is joining the highly anticipated Harry Potter TV series as the wizarding world's celebrity-turned-Hogwarts instructor Gilderoy Lockhart.
X-Men star Nicholas Hoult was originally cast in the second series earlier this month but has now left due to scheduling issues, according to HBO.
Best known for playing Jon Snow in Game of Thrones, Harington also appears in BBC and HBO financial drama Industry. The star previously voiced Lockhart in an audio version of Harry Potter.

"I'm a huge Potter fan. I've got to be honest, he's one of my favourite characters," Harington told Collider, external. "So, to be offered to play him is a real dream. I've had a taste of him [in the audiobook] and felt my way around him. He's just a wonderful creation."

articles.title: Nandamuri Balakrishna, Sunny Deol, Nayanthara Lead Zee Studios’ Multilingual 2026-27 Slate (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: India’s Zee Studios has unveiled a diversified multilingual, multi-genre content slate for 2026-27, spanning Hindi, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Gujarati and Kannada cinema.
body: The portfolio brings together commercial entertainers, action spectacles, thrillers, mythology-driven epics and regionally rooted stories.

In the Tamil language, the studio is backing “Hi,” starring Nayanthara and Kavin and directed by Vishnu Edavan, and “Sathyavan Savithri,” starring Keerthy Suresh and Mysskin and directed by Praveen S. Vijaay. The Kannada-language entry “Anna From Mexico” stars Dhananjaya, Reeshma Nanaiah, Umashree, Rangayana Raghu and Sadhu Kokila under director Shankar Guru. Zee Studios has also stepped into the Gujarati-language market with “Tom and Cherry,” starring Siddharth Randeria and Dhanya Doshi and directed by Dharmessh Mehta.

Marathi-language cinema forms another pillar of the strategy, building on the Indian National Film Award-winning “Aatmapamphlet.” The new slate includes “Jhep,” directed by Priyadarshan Jadhav; “Phulwara,” starring Priyadarshini Indalkar and directed by Ravi Jadhav; “Jogai,” starring Jitendra Joshi and Sajiri Joshi and directed by Vishal Modhave; and “Maan.”
The genre mix extends further with “Silaa,” starring Harshvardhan Rane, Sadia Khateeb and Karanveer Mehra and directed by Omung Kumar.

articles.title: Songs created by AI banned from Australia's music charts
articles.summary: The move comes weeks after a DJ admitted using AI to remix a Madonna song that topped the Australian charts.
body: Songs that are largely or wholly created by AI have been banned from Australia's music charts.
From this week, all releases must be "substantially human made" to be eligible.
The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) said the new code would help "promote the human nature of artistry".

It follows a controversy around a cover of Madonna's Like A Prayer by Australian DJ Josh Fawaz which recently topped the ARIA dance singles chart and peaked at number 2 on the country's overall chart.

articles.title: Hilary Strong Steps Down as CEO of John Gore Studios
articles.summary: The company will be "joining forces with its U.S.-based sister company, The John Gore Organization," in a rejig, with both under the executive leadership of owner and founder Gore.
body: London-based film and TV studio John Gore Studios, which is behind the likes of the Toronto-bound Onwards and Sideways, with Laura Linney and Rhys Ifans starring as two people being diagnosed with Parkinson’s, said on Tuesday that Hilary Strong is stepping down as CEO and that it will reorganize.

British-born Gore, a two-time Emmy and Olivier award winner, has served as executive chairman of John Gore Studios, with Strong, whose previous roles included chief at Agatha Christie Ltd. and commercial director at Hat Trick Productions, as CEO.

articles.title: 87 Years Ago Today: One Of The Most Beloved Movies Ever Made Opened Nationwide—and Barely Broke Even
articles.summary: Even 87 years after its original theatrical release, The Wizard of Oz remains one of the most beloved movies ever... though it took a while to get there.
body: Loosely based on L. Frank Baum's 1900 book "The Wonderful Wizard of Oz," the film had an infamously long road to the big screen. Victor Fleming is the movie's credited director, but he was only one of several filmmakers who oversaw the project. Indeed, it's well-known among film historians that King Vidor directed some of the film's Kansas-set sepia-toned scenes, while Norman Taurog oversaw some of its color tests, Mervyn LeRoy helmed some transitional scenes, and George Cukor and Richard Thorpe each briefly sat in the director's chair. Reading about the production of "The Wizard of Oz" is a litany of horrors, and it's astonishing the film got made at all.
And, perhaps surprisingly, "The Wizard of Oz" initially underperformed at the box office. As noted by the AFI, the movie actually lost money at first.

Per AFI, "The Wizard of Oz" had a, for its time, large $2.77 million budget but lost about a million dollars during its original theatrical run due primarily to its advertising and distribution costs. As a result, the movie didn't recoup its losses until it was re-released in theaters from 1948 to 1949. It had a long path to break even.

articles.title: Meet Mestiza, the Female Duo From Spain Mixing Flamenco and Electronic Music
articles.summary: Belah and Pitty discuss their music and aesthetics, upcoming shows in London and New York, leaning into the "almost ritualistic" nature of electronic music, and the visual, cinematic side of their creativity.
body: Spanish DJs Belah Sánchez and Patricia “Pitty” Bernad had their own careers. But in 2021, they teamed up under the moniker Mestiza. Since then, the Spanish DJ and producer duo has been finding a growing fan base with its combination of electronic music with flamenco influences.

After playing Coachella earlier this year, this fall, the women behind Mestiza are bringing their high-energy act, as part of its Sacro event series, to New York, where they will rock the Brooklyn outdoor venue Creekside – Under The K Bridge, and London, where the duo will bring its sounds to the legendary Roundhouse in Camden on Oct. 30.

THR, in an email Q&A, asked Mestiza about the duo’s history, music and aesthetics, their respect for flamenco, which comes from Andalusia in southern Spain, and what’s next for them, including a possible cinema project.
How and when did you two decide to become a duo rather than continuing your solo work?
